newsitem.title: CHINA: China Chongqing Changan sees H1 net up.
newsitem.headline: China Chongqing Changan sees H1 net up.

text.p: China's Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd would probably post a 23 percent year-on-year jump in its first-half net profits, a company official said on Monday.
Unaudited net earnings were expected to reach about 110 million yuan for the first six months, compared with the 89.1 million in the same period in 1995, the official said.
Changan was on its way to achieving its target of 232 million yuan for 1997 net profits, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
"In previous years we made more profits in the second half than the first, and I am confident we will reach this year's target," he said.
The forecast 1997 net profits, based on international accounting standards, compared with 202.83 million yuan posted in 1996.
The official attributed the profit surge to a steady increase in car sales, with production expected to increase to 80,000 cars in 1997 from 70,400 last year. He gave no further details.
Analysts said they had expected Changan to perform strongly this year.
"I think when the interim report comes out the net will be even higher, maybe at 130 million yuan," said an analyst at J&A Securities specialising in the car industry.
"Changan's mini-van is doing very well and is likely to be popular in the market for another 10 to 15 years," he said.
Changan's B share closed Monday at HK$3.04, up HK$0.11.
"I don't think the results will have a significant impact on the share price unless they veer from expectations," the analyst said.
